name: TBILLPRICE
description: TBILLPRICE returns the price per $100 face value of a Treasury bill based on its discount rate.
tldr: Calculates the price of a Treasury bill per $100 face value.

basicExample.explanation: A 6-month T-bill with a 5% discount rate is priced at $97.50 per $100 face value.

howItWorks: TBILLPRICE calculates the price using the formula 100 * (1 - discount * days to maturity / 360). Treasury bills use a 360-day year for pricing.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Maturity must be within one year of settlement.
Discount is entered as a decimal.

commonErrors.cause: Maturity is more than one year after settlement or discount is invalid.
commonErrors.fix: Verify dates are within one year and discount is valid.
Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TBILLPRICE works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between TBILLPRICE and PRICEDISC?
faq.answer: TBILLPRICE is specifically for Treasury bills with a 360-day year. PRICEDISC is more general and can use different bases.

faq.question: When is TBILLPRICE used?
faq.answer: It is used for pricing US Treasury bills.
